description: This document outlines functional gaps, design issues, and recommended improvements to strengthen maintainability, accuracy, and scalability of the parser.

list: Dynamic routing between JSON and Parquet parsing based on file size threshold.
Recursive normalization of nested data structures.
Support for JSON arrays, single objects, and NDJSON inputs.
Type inference system providing consistent schema representation.
S3 interaction via signed URLs and range-based downloads.
The function `ParseJsonToParquet` is defined but contains no implementation for Parquet conversion.
In `parseNDJSON`, nested objects are not properly normalized; they are represented by static placeholders.
Column alignment logic may break when rows have mismatched or new keys appearing after initial schema creation.
Channel closing order in `ParseJsonToJson` may lead to premature closure or blocking behavior under some conditions.
Implement a streaming parser for both JSON and NDJSON to avoid loading entire data into memory at once.
Refactor normalization to maintain schema consistency dynamically across rows.
Make the 50 MB cutoff value configurable through environment variables or runtime arguments.
Use buffered uploads to improve performance during S3 PUT requests.
Introduce error recovery and partial upload continuation mechanisms.
Add unit tests for inferType, detectJSONType, normalizeJSON, and parseNDJSON with diverse input samples.
Include integration tests for S3 I/O, validating both small and large file workflows.
Simulate malformed or partial NDJSON input to verify scanner error handling.
Benchmark normalization performance on nested and irregular JSON documents.
Integrate Apache Arrow or equivalent library for Parquet conversion in `ParseJsonToParquet`.
Expand type inference to include date, null, and mixed-type field support.
Refactor schema definition to use maps instead of slices for O(1) key lookup.
Implement incremental upload progress reporting for long-running operations.
